name: media
whenToEnable: Store, track, and enrich media — images (R2 or Cloudflare Images), video (R2 or Cloudflare Stream), audio and documents (R2). Uploads use direct-upload URLs, so bytes never proxy through your Worker. Every record carries its owner, the organization in force, and a visibility — private, organization or public — and a non-public Images or Stream asset is delivered only through short-lived signed URLs. Duplicate detection stays inside the tenant. Opt in per type to AI alt text, transcription, and text extraction. Records live in D1. R2 presigning runs through @pithy-sh/storage's ObjectStore seam pointed at MEDIA_BUCKET, so media owns no bucket mechanics and none of storage's tables or routes come with it. Storage credentials and signing keys are read through @pithy-sh/secrets, so the secrets capability is required; writes need an identity, so add auth too, and organization if records belong to teams.
scaffold: Ensure the secrets capability is provisioned (`pithy add secrets` then `pithy secrets provision`) — the CF API token, the R2 credentials and the signing keys are stored and read through @pithy-sh/secrets.

Create an R2 S3 access-key pair (R2 → Manage API tokens) and an API token with Images and Stream permissions. Cloudflare exposes no API for minting an R2 key pair, so this pair is yours to create — pithy stores and rotates it, but cannot mint it.

Run `pithy media provision` — it creates the R2 bucket, writes the per-environment secrets, reads the Images URL-signing key and creates a Stream signing key, and deploys the media enrichment worker hosting the four Workflows for each environment. `media-storage-credentials` holds your Images + Stream API token; `media-r2-credentials` holds the R2 key pair and that environment's bucket, and is read by @pithy-sh/storage's ObjectStore, which media presigns through. It refuses while an Images variant is set to `neverRequireSignedURLs`, because that variant would serve a private image to anyone. Pass the credentials with `--api-token`, `--r2-access-key-id`, and `--r2-secret-access-key`, or set `R2_CREDENTIALS` in `.dev.vars`. Every step is idempotent; re-run it freely.

Add the `DB` (D1) and `MEDIA_BUCKET` (R2) bindings to each wrangler.jsonc env. Add the enrichment Workflow bindings your app dispatches to on finalize: `MEDIA_IMAGE_TO_TEXT`, `MEDIA_AUDIO_TRANSCRIBE`, `MEDIA_VIDEO_TRANSCRIBE`, `MEDIA_DOC_EXTRACT`.

Set the `delivery` config (public identifiers) so delivery URLs can be built: `imagesAccountHash` (Cloudflare Images) and `streamCustomerCode` (Cloudflare Stream). A non-public record's URL comes from `GET /media/:id/url`, signed and short-lived. `r2PublicBaseUrl` serves every key in a public bucket, so it is refused unless `visibility.allowed` is `["public"]`.

Decide who may see what: `visibility: { default: "private", allowed: ["private", "organization", "public"] }` in `media({ ... })`. `["private", "organization"]` means nothing can ever be published. Records written before this release are private and system-owned until you assign owners.

Enable AI enrichment per type in `media({ ... })` in pithy.config.ts — `images.imageToText`, `video.transcribe`, `audio.transcribe`, `documents.extractText` (extraction runs for pdf/doc/docx only). Each is independently opt-in and a no-op (no cost) when off. Override any model with the type's `model` field.

Writes require an authenticated caller. Add the auth capability (`pithy add auth`) so `c.var.auth` is populated; without it only public records can be read. Add the organization capability to scope records to teams, and give some role `media:manage` so an organization can clean up after somebody who left.
Share a record with one person, or put one on legal hold, with `media({ permission })` — a hook asked on every read and write that answers `allow`, `deny` or `default`.

Extend a media record with your own fields — tags, an album — by passing an `extend` Zod object to `media({ extend })`. The extra fields become real D1 columns (a generated migration) from that one schema. The owner and organization are already there.

configOptions.describe: Who may read a media record: `default` is the level an upload gets when it names none, `allowed` every level a write may name. Drop `public` from `allowed` and nothing can ever be published.
